children: , the networking and cybersecurity giant, slipped approximately 0.5% to $108.865 Thursday as Huawei's federal criminal trial opened in Brooklyn. Prosecutors accused the Chinese technology company of conspiring to steal trade secrets from five U.S. businesses, including source code for Cisco's router operating system.

The case stretches well beyond intellectual property. Federal prosecutors also alleged sanctions and financial-system violations tied to Iran, while Huawei rejected the charges and described the disputed activity as legitimate business conduct or isolated employee behavior. The trial could run for roughly three months. Cisco is not prosecuting the case, and investors have no disclosed financial recovery to price into the shares.

The bigger earnings engine sits inside Cisco's AI pipeline. The company booked $9.3 billion of fiscal 2026 AI orders, equal to about 14.7% of its $63.33 billion in annual revenue, and expects AI revenue to climb from approximately $4 billion to $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027. The picture adds a valuation warning: Cisco trades 46.56% above its $74.28 GF Value estimate. The Huawei trial may reopen an old wound, but converting that AI backlog into profitable growth is the test that matters now.

title: Cisco Slips as Huawei Source-Code Claims Reach Trial
